subject: Opsly onboarding: model profiles, context depth, and capacity estimate
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@opsly.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@opsly.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ready to kick off Redwood onboarding — context & traffic details

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to get Redwood integrated for our in-app assistant. Attached is a brief questionnaire the engineers asked us to complete (I attached answers inline to speed things up). Before we schedule the technical kickoff, two quick asks so we can align expectations: 

- What model sizes and context lengths you typically recommend for a customer like us (conversational UI + short-document summarization)?
- Rough per-minute and per-day token budget we should expect for a 5k MAU pilot with heavy peak usage (peak 10% of users active concurrently).

I attached the questionnaire and included some initial usage numbers below. If you need more granular traffic (session length distribution, message length histogram), tell me what format you prefer and I can pull it from our analytics.

Attached: [Attachment: opsly-questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Quick snapshot (Opsly pilot):
- MAU: 5,000
- Avg sessions/day per MAU: 0.8
- Avg messages per session: 6 (mix of prompts + short documents)
- Avg tokens per message: 45 (prompt) / 350 (when user pastes a short doc to summarize)
- Peak concurrent users target for pilot: 500

Appreciate any early guidance — we want to avoid a surprise spike on day one.

Best,
Samir
Engineering Lead, Opsly
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Samir Khan <samir@opsly.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ready to kick off Redwood onboarding — context & traffic details

Samir — thanks for the numbers and the questionnaire, this is exactly what we need to size the pilot. High level recommendations up front, then a quick ask for one extra data point.

Summary guidance (pilot, 5k MAU):
- Model shortlist (we recommend validating two flavors in parallel):
  1) MPT-7B-instruct / llama-7B-compat (4k context) — lowest-cost, good for short conversational flows and quick summaries.
  2) MPT-13B-extended or a 13B quantized variant (8k context) — for sessions that include pasted short docs (300–1,000 tokens) plus multi-turn history.
- Context recommendation: start pilot on 4k for conversation-only flows and enable an 8k variant for summary paths (route by endpoint).
- Token estimate (pilot steady-state): ~6M tokens/day; peak burst planning: we size for ~12–15M tokens/day equivalent to handle 24-hour bursty patterns.
- Operational levers: prefix caching for repeated system prompts, short-term KV cache for in-session context to reduce repeated tokens, and batching at the edge for concurrent small requests.

One extra item: can you send a CSV with the session histogram (session length in messages) and a small sample of typical pasted-doc lengths? If you can’t, we’ll use the averages you sent but will add a 30% safety margin.

Next steps I’m proposing:
- Priyom (CS Solutions) will produce a quick capacity workbook and recommended routing rules (model -> endpoint mapping) for your pilot.
- Schedule 60-minute tech kickoff this week to walk the team through the plan and confirm security/privilege needs.

I’ve attached a short write-up of the model tradeoffs we use internally for this use case.

Attachments: [Attachment: model-profile-recs.md (Markdown, 6KB)], [Attachment: opsly-questionnaire.pdf referenced]

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Ready to kick off Redwood onboarding — model shortlist & capacity workbook

Samir / team — attaching the capacity workbook and a short runbook with routing suggestions. Key items and assumptions are below; the workbook has scenario tabs (baseline, +30% traffic, and high-burst).

High-level sizing assumptions we used:
- MAU 5k, sessions/day per MAU: 0.8 (as provided)
- Messages/session: 6, with a 1:5 ratio of short conversational prompts to long summary requests
- Avg tokens: conversation prompts 45 tokens; long-summary requests average 450 tokens input + 250 tokens generation

Baseline token estimate (day):
- Conversation traffic: 5k * 0.8 * 6 * (45 + 60 avg generation) = ~3.24M tokens/day
- Summary traffic: 5k * 0.8 * 6 * (1/6 of messages are long) * (450 + 250) = ~2.6M tokens/day
- Total baseline: ~5.9M tokens/day — matches Soojin's rough ~6M/day estimate.

Peak / provisioning guidance:
- Provision for 2x baseline across Dedicated pool during pilot start (handles bursty adoption and concurrent spike to 10% active users).
- Use 4k context variant for conversational endpoints; route summary endpoints to 8k context model.
- Quantized 13B variant for summaries yields ~35–40% cost savings vs FP16 13B while retaining quality in internal tests.

Attachments: [Attachment: cs_workload_estimate.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)],
[Attachment: onboarding-runbook.md (MD, 8KB)]

Operational notes / quick wins:
- Enable per-route caching TTL of 15s for identical system prompts to cut repeated tokens on quick UI actions.
- Implement rate-limited fallbacks to a smaller model during sustained overloads (e.g., > 60s queue time).
- Instrument token-level metrics in the first week to refine generation length assumptions.

I’ll join the kickoff — propose Wed 22nd at 11:00 PT or Thu 23rd at 10:00 PT. Which works?

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
